title: The Gāyatrī at midday: Sāvitrī in Rudra’s form

words.meaning: whose faces are pearl-pale, golden, grey and white

words.context: M spells it त्रिक्षणा (for त्रीक्षणा, tri + īkṣaṇa)

words.meaning: a young woman in her prime

words.context: the series of the three dhyānas: rājasī (morning), tāmasī (midday), sāttvikī (evening)

samasa.vigraha: खट्वाङ्गं च अभयं च शूलकं च
samasa.meaning: the khaṭvāṅga, the fearlessness-gesture and the trident

translation.literal: The pearl-pale, gold, grey and white-faced, three-eyed, sky-going one, white-bodied at midday, the fair young woman, whose nature is truth, of tamas; holding the khaṭvāṅga, the fearlessness-gesture and the trident, the rudrākṣa rosary — Umā, Sāvitrī, riding the bull, bringer of dissolution, in the form of Śrī Rudra, I worship.
translation.readable: At midday I worship the goddess as Sāvitrī: white-bodied, a young woman, three-eyed, moving in the sky, her faces pale as pearl, golden, grey and white; she holds the skull-staff, the trident and a rudrākṣa rosary and shows the gesture of fearlessness; she is Umā, rides the bull, brings things to their end, and has the form of Rudra.

meaning: The midday form of the goddess of the Gāyatrī, one of three dhyāna verses in the Mylapore prayoga, one for each service. At dawn she is a girl with Brahmā’s attributes, at midday a young woman with Rudra’s, at dusk an old woman with Viṣṇu’s: the three times of day are mapped onto creation, dissolution and preservation, and onto the three guṇas. Here she is Sāvitrī and Umā, white, three-eyed, riding Rudra’s bull, holding the khaṭvāṅga (a staff topped with a skull), the trident and a rudrākṣa rosary.
in_the_rite: Step dhyāna of the Gāyatrī japa, midday service only (the Mylapore prayoga), after the general verse muktā-vidruma. S does not have the three time-specific verses.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Śārdūlavikrīḍita metre: four pādas of nineteen syllables, here written as two lines. Only M has this verse.
